data:
Status: released v0.1.0.
Interpolation, splines and smoothing in pure Go (CGO_ENABLED=0), validated against SciPy and NumPy.
go get github.com/go-approx/interp@v0.1.0 import "github.com/go-approx/interp" s, _ := interp.NewCubicSpline(x, y, "not-a-knot") // scipy CubicSpline, MATLAB spline v := s.At(2.5); d := s.Derivative(1).At(2.5); area := s.Integrate(0, 4) b, _ := interp.MakeInterpSpline(x, y, 5, nil) // make_interp_spline sm, _ := interp.MakeSplrep(x, y, 3, 0.05, nil) // FITPACK smoothing spline
data.differences-from-scipy#Differences from: Errors are returned, not raised, and no function panics on input. NewInterp1D rejects NaN in x. numpy.interp is reproduced with math.FMA because NumPy’s C loop is compiled with fused multiply-add on arm64; every other kernel rounds each product before summing. Tensor-product splines are solved one axis at a time. RectBivariateSpline smoothing (s > 0) and the periodic smoothing spline of make_splrep are not provided.
data.gaps#Gaps:
Scattered-data interpolation (Delaunay, natural neighbour, RBF) is a later work item. There is no periodic smoothing spline, no parametric splines (make_splprep), no make_smoothing_spline, no MATLAB interp2 cubic kernel, no complex-valued data, no N-dimensional y, and PPoly.roots and BSpline.roots are not provided.
Source: go-approx/interp, BSD-3-Clause.
data.performance#Performance:
docs/perf.md has the table: construction and evaluation at 10^3 to 10^6 points, Go against SciPy on one core, interleaved rounds, with the load average of the host.
The README, measured 2026-10-19 (load 3–5), reports interp faster than SciPy on PCHIP, Akima/makima, cubic evaluation, periodic cubic construction, nearest-neighbour interp1d, make_splrep, least-squares splines and every RegularGridInterpolator construction.
Open defects, still slower than the reference (from the README): splrep against SciPy’s legacy FITPACK splrep (0.33–0.38x), RectBivariateSpline construction (0.84–0.88x), np.interp and linear interp1d evaluation (0.86–0.89x), quintic B-spline evaluation (0.92–0.97x) and not-a-knot cubic construction from 10^5 points (0.92x).
data.verification#Verification:
The reference tools are SciPy 1.18.1 and NumPy 2.5.4, run as oracles from Go by the tag-gated harness oracle_test.go. The harness generates the inputs and writes the answers to testdata/*.json; the ordinary tests read them and need no Python.
Inputs include the edge cases: 1, 2 and 3 points, duplicate and unsorted x, NaN and Inf in x and y, queries outside the range and exactly on the nodes, nodes clustered over 14 orders of magnitude, offsets of 1e8, spans of 1e-9, values of 1e150 and 1e-290, mismatched lengths, invalid boundary conditions and knots, and n = 1e5 and 1e6. Where SciPy raises, the Go constructor returns an error and the fixture says so.
Octave is not installed on the build host, so MATLAB/Octave semantics are implemented from the MathWorks documentation and checked through the SciPy objects that implement the same maths, not against Octave.
data.what-is-provided#What is provided: here SciPy / NumPy NewInterp1D (Linear, Nearest, NearestUp, Previous, Next) interpolate.interp1d Interp numpy.interp Interp1 (linear nearest next previous pchip cubic spline makima) the matching classes; MATLAB interp1 NewCubicSpline, NewCubicSplineBC (not-a-knot, natural, clamped, periodic, prescribed derivatives), PPoly CubicSpline, PPoly NewCubicHermite, NewPchip, NewAkima CubicHermiteSpline, PchipInterpolator, Akima1DInterpolator / makima MakeInterpSpline, BSpline, NewDesignMatrix make_interp_spline, BSpline, BSpline.design_matrix MakeLsqSpline make_lsq_spline MakeSplrep (FITPACK smoothing: automatic knots, smoothing factor, weights, user knots) make_splrep, splrep, UnivariateSpline NewRGI, Interpn (linear, nearest, slinear, cubic, quintic) RegularGridInterpolator, interpn MakeNdInterp, NdBSpline (tensor-product splines) make_ndbspl, NdBSpline NewBicubic RectBivariateSpline(..., s=0) The README has the full table with the MATLAB equivalents.

data:
Status: released v0.1.0.
Polynomials in pure Go (CGO_ENABLED=0): evaluation, arithmetic, least-squares fitting, roots, and the Chebyshev, Legendre, Hermite, HermiteE and Laguerre bases, with the semantics of numpy.polyfit, numpy.roots, the numpy.poly1d helpers and the numpy.polynomial package.
go get github.com/go-approx/poly@v0.1.0 import "github.com/go-approx/poly" fit, _ := poly.Polyfit(x, y, 3, nil) // highest degree first, like np.polyfit r, _ := poly.Roots(fit.Coef) // companion-matrix eigenvalues v := poly.Polyval(fit.Coef, 0.5) // Horner; PolyvalComp is compensated s, _, _ := poly.FitSeries(poly.Chebyshev, x, y, 8, nil) // lowest degree first, like numpy.polynomial y0, _ := s.Val(0.3) Coefficient order differs between the two families, as in NumPy: the poly1d family is highest degree first, the numpy.polynomial family lowest degree first.
data.gaps#Gaps:
float64 only; one-dimensional coefficient and data arrays; a single integer degree (no list of degrees as np.polyfit allows in 2.x). No complex-coefficient Polyval or fits. No numpy.polynomial.Polynomial (power-basis series) class beyond the poly1d functions. Conv is not bit-identical to np.convolve. No Octave oracle.
Source: go-approx/poly, BSD-3-Clause.
data.performance#Performance: docs/perf.md has the comparison of Go against NumPy on one core, interleaved rounds. It is only meaningful on an idle machine; the table states the load it was taken at. The Householder QR of the fits runs its inner products and updates on go-simd/floats (Dot, Axpy: assembly generated by go-asmgen), and the Vandermonde and series design matrices are built in cache-sized row blocks.
data.verification#Verification:
The reference is NumPy 2.5.4 (SciPy 1.18.1 installed alongside), run as an oracle from Go. A tagged test (-tags oracle) generates the fixtures in testdata/ (deterministic inputs, large cases regenerated from their seed); the ordinary tests read them and need no Python. Octave is not installed on the host, so no Octave oracle was run.
Measured against NumPy, as the README reports:
quantity result Polyval, Polyder, Polyint, Polyadd, Polysub, Deconv, PolyFromRoots 3434 of 3434 values bit-identical Conv, Polymul 229 of 917 bit-identical; max error 0.90 eps relative to the sum of abs(a_i b_j) (NumPy’s convolve uses a different summation order) PolyvalComp worst error / theoretical bound = 0.00095; more accurate than Horner at 677 of 780 points each of the 5 bases: Val, Vander, Der, Int, Series.Val/Der/Int 10016 of 10016 values bit-identical Roots 8 of 24 cases identical in value and order; well-conditioned random degree <= 50: max positional error 4e-15 Polyfit 78 fits; coefficient deviation at most 1.67 conditioning units The bit-identical rows hold on every architecture because every product that feeds a sum is rounded explicitly, which forbids fused multiply-add. The least-squares fits are not bit-identical across architectures: their QR runs on go-simd/floats, whose Dot adds in SIMD lanes in an order that depends on the vector width. The fit tolerances hold on every architecture CI runs.
Gates: gofmt -l . empty, go vet, go test -race, 100.0% statement coverage with -coverpkg=./..., and a CI that runs Linux, macOS, Windows, arm64, qemu riscv64/loong64/ppc64le/s390x/arm, 386, compiles every GOOS/GOARCH and runs govulncheck.
data.what-is-provided#What is provided: here NumPy Polyval, PolyvalAll np.polyval PolyvalComp, PolyvalCompAll (none) compensated Horner, Graillat-Langlois-Louvet 2009 Polyder, Polyint np.polyder, np.polyint Conv, Deconv, Polymul, Polyadd, Polysub np.convolve, np.polydiv, np.polymul, np.polyadd, np.polysub PolyFromRoots, PolyFromComplexRoots np.poly Polyfit (weights, rcond, covariance scaled or unscaled, rank) np.polyfit Roots np.roots Basis (Chebyshev, Legendre, Hermite, HermiteE, Laguerre) with Val, Vander, Der, Int, RootsBasis, FitBasis chebval, chebvander, chebder, chebint, chebroots, chebfit and the leg, herm, herme, lag equivalents Series (NewSeries, FitSeries, Val, Der, Int, Roots), MapParms, MapDomain, GetDomain numpy.polynomial.Chebyshev etc. with domain/window mapping
